hints.title: As-Of Date Pricing Resolution
hints.text: Determine the price of each product as of 2019-08-16, falling back to a default baseline price of ten if no price update preceded that date.

hints.title: Distinct Product Union with Latest Subquery
hints.text: Left join all distinct products against the most recent price record on or before the target date, replacing nulls with ten.

hints.title: Price As-Of Query Blueprint
hints.text: select p.product_id, coalesce(t.new_price, 10) as price from (select distinct product_id from Products) p left join (select product_id, new_price from Products where (product_id, change_date) in (select product_id, max(change_date) from Products where change_date <= "2019-08-16" group by product_id)) t on p.product_id = t.product_id.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
SELECT p.product_id, COALESCE(t.new_price, 10) AS price
FROM (
    SELECT DISTINCT product_id
    FROM Products
) p
LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT product_id, new_price
    FROM Products
    WHERE (product_id, change_date) IN (
        SELECT product_id, MAX(change_date)
        FROM Products
        WHERE change_date <= '2019-08-16'
        GROUP BY product_id
    )
) t ON p.product_id = t.product_id;
```

variables: P: number of price modification records
complexity.notes: Finding max change dates per product followed by left join executes in linear-logarithmic time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Simple inner join drops products whose initial price changes took place after the cutoff date.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Distinct product universe left joined against latest price subquery cleanly establishes baseline fallback.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Preserving all distinct products with default price 10 using LEFT JOIN and COALESCE.

solutions.code:
import pandas as pd

def price_at_given_date(products: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    all_prods = pd.DataFrame({'product_id': products['product_id'].unique()})
    valid = products[products['change_date'] <= '2019-08-16']
    idx = valid.groupby('product_id')['change_date'].idxmax()
    latest = valid.loc[idx, ['product_id', 'new_price']].rename(columns={'new_price': 'price'})
    res = all_prods.merge(latest, on='product_id', how='left')
    res['price'] = res['price'].fillna(10).astype(int)
    return res
solutions.approach: Pandas Sub-Date Idxmax and Outer Merge with Default Fill
